identityAndDescriptor.nativeTypes: Private validated SpoolIdentity and ClockDescriptor, constructed from native-owned values, not deserialized directly into a trusted capability. Every disk schema separately uses deny_unknown_fields and strict nested owner decoding. No browser-supplied filesystem path, format name or arbitrary MIME string.
identity: fixed provider youtube and branch youtubeVp9AacRawV1
canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID jobId, requestId, receiverId, sourceId and documentId
documentEpoch and sourceGeneration are distinct positive u64 values
exact11-character canonical videoId and24-character UC channelId
full Manual or Scheduled RecordingOwner; no owner identity inferred from job UUID
identityAndDescriptor.scheduledOwner: Reuse live::RecordingOwner semantics in memory, without modifying its shared serde behavior. Strict persisted owner is a separate closed local representation. Scheduled schedule_id equals the descriptor channelId; broadcast_key equals videoId; run_id is canonical UUID and owner generation is positive. The complete owner, including run and generation, is part of equality for every append/seal and recovery expectation.
identityAndDescriptor.descriptor: Exactly two fixed typed tracks: ordinal0 video WebM VP9 and ordinal1 audio MP4 AAC-LC. Immutable segments mode, default appendWindow and exactly zero timestampOffset for both; fixed enums instead of extensible strings. Integer video TimestampScaleNs and AAC timescale each lie in1..1,000,000,000; these are metadata bounds, not media admission. Nonzero/changing offsets are refused rather than independently zeroing tracks. Native receipt elapsedMs is separate from source clock and must never become PTS or chat evidence.
identityAndDescriptor.authorityBoundary: The disabled writer validates identity consistency, not live website authentication, current native receiver ownership or recording consent. A future explicitly reviewed integration must construct it only while holding existing exact source/document/epoch/owner admission and active-job ownership, with a shared cancellation guard. Passing a syntactically valid identity is not recording permission.
identityAndDescriptor.mutations: append and seal require exact SpoolIdentity equality. A foreign identity is rejected before file/state mutation and must not poison another owner's writer. A protocol or I/O failure from the matching identity permanently closes its write admission. No identity or descriptor setter exists.

ownedFiles.layout: Use storage::job_dir(trusted_native_media_root, youtube, jobId), validate the existing root/provider parents, then create only that previously absent UUID job directory with create_dir, never create_dir_all over an unknown path. Fixed new files are proof.json, video.raw, audio.raw and journal.jsonl. No other path is accepted by the public-to-module API. The directory must not already exist, including a previous failed attempt.
ownedFiles.creation: Check every ancestor is a real local directory with no reparse/symlink, reject UNC/device/ADS/traversal forms, and fail on metadata/open errors rather than treating them as absence. Hold directory handles without delete sharing on Windows. Open every fixed file create_new with read/write, read-only sharing and OPEN_REPARSE_POINT; retain handles through writer lifetime. Check regular type, file identity and single link at opening and before/after mutation. Recovery holds read-only handles denying concurrent write/delete, using the same path and identity rules.
ownedFiles.proof: Create_new proof.json has a closed versioned schema, at most8192 bytes, exact identity/descriptor, fixed filenames and fixed limits. Write and sync it before admitting appends. A journal header stores version and SHA256 of the exact proof bytes. Raw files and the header are synced before create_new returns. Proof is immutable; no JSON replacement or path rename is required in phase1.
ownedFiles.failure: Any partial construction or write failure leaves every created file intact. Do not remove empty files, retry into the same directory, truncate an uncommitted tail or replace a proof. Owned directory/file identity is checked again at seal and recovery. Tests may remove only their isolated TempDir through its ordinary fixture lifecycle, never user media.
ownedFiles.durabilityQualification: ACK follows successful File::sync_all calls on raw and journal handles using existing Windows local persistence conventions. No claim is made that application code can override lying storage hardware or guarantee arbitrary power-loss filesystem metadata behavior. File/path substitution is prevented by held handles and checked identity, not a check-then-close assumption.

limits.nonFinalChunk: Exactly131072 bytes. Final chunks contain1..131072 bytes. Zero-length chunks, empty logical appends and a redundant empty final marker are invalid.
limits.explanation: At most1,100,000 receipt rows, each at most1024 bytes including LF, and independently at most1GiB for the entire journal including header/seal. Reserve one1024-byte seal row before admitting receipts. Checked counters/arithmetic; one incomplete logical append globally. Memory is current128KiB chunk, one1KiB row, bounded per-track/hash state and one last receipt, never32MiB or an hours-long journal.
limits.space: Before creation require1GiB plus bounded overhead. Before every raw write check the sum of exact chunk+serialized receipt+1024-byte seal headroom+1GiB. Recheck immediately before header/receipt/seal writes for that write+remaining seal headroom+reserve. Unknown/low space is terminal with source preserved. This is not a reservation against other processes; no automatic rollover/cap increase.
limits.clock: Use native monotonic elapsed time for the live24h ceiling and receipt elapsedMs; sampled once per prospective receipt, monotonically nondecreasing and at most86400000. Recovery validates stored bounds but does not mistake a persisted elapsed count for wall-clock continuity or source media time. OS file calls have no asserted hard completion deadline; future integration must keep them off the UI thread.

journalProtocol.format: UTF-8 JSONL, compact closed tagged records, lowercase64-hex SHA256 fields, integer-only counters, no arbitrary strings. Header binds the exact proof SHA256. Receipt global sequence starts0; track is the closed ordinal enum, appendIndex and chunkIndex are per-track ordered, offset/length are exact contiguous bytes in that track's raw file, finalChunk marks logical completion, elapsedMs is native receipt time. Include payloadSha256 and previousRecordSha256; the latter hashes the exact preceding complete line including LF, starting at the header. Seal binds the last line hash and both committed track lengths/stream SHA256 folds, next append counters and any incomplete logical append.
appendOrder: Check exact identity, writer-open/cancel/time state, fixed track, per-track append/chunk index, single active logical append, size/count/file guards and sufficient space; serialize the proposed bounded receipt before mutation.
Write the chunk at the exact committed raw offset on its held file; write_all failure poisons the writer. Do not seek past a failed tail or retry the write.
sync_all the raw handle. A flush/sync failure is terminal and cannot ACK.
Recheck cancellation and file identity before committing the journal receipt; an observed cancellation leaves a preserved uncommitted raw tail and no ACK.

Check receipt-space reserve, append exactly one complete bounded LF-terminated receipt, then sync_all the journal. A partial write or sync error poisons even if the bytes happen to be present on disk.

Only after both syncs update the bounded committed counters, streaming raw hashes and exact-last receipt. Recheck cancellation before returning an ACK; cancellation here means committed-but-unacknowledged data, never rollback.
Return a durability-only ACK containing fixed receipt identity/committed offsets. Do not publish media or mark progress as playable.
journalProtocol.ordering: Per-track appendIndex begins0 and advances only on finalChunk. chunkIndex begins0 for each logical append. A partial logical append excludes any other track/append until its final chunk; max32MiB is checked with subtraction/checked addition. Same-owner missing/reordered chunks, changed descriptor/source, reused index with changed bytes and bound violations close this writer's admission, preserving all committed data.
journalProtocol.retry: Only the single global most recent fully committed receipt may repeat, with identical full identity/track/index/chunk/final/length/hash, current native authorization/cancellation fence, intact held file identities and known successful original persistence. Recheck all current guards before ACK. Same committed position with duplicate=true, no write/counter change. A last valid receipt that exactly reached a byte/count ceiling can re-ACK before any terminal cap failure is latched, because it needs no new capacity. Older receipts and any latched cap/poison/revocation/seal/expiry fail. Crash-after-sync-before-ACK is inspected read-only; never infer delivery or recreate writable state.
journalProtocol.errorModel: Closed fixed error categories distinguish invalid identity/proof, order, bounds, cancelled, expired, low space, unsafe path, I/O and corrupt journal. Do not retain arbitrary OS messages, URLs or media bytes in public errors/logs. A matching-owner mutation failure latches the first terminal error; later calls never overwrite it with success. No generic retry framework.

sealAndDrop.seal: seal(&mut self, identity, cause) validates full identity before changing state; a foreign call returns an error without consuming/dropping or closing the legitimate writer. The exact owner then closes admission and enters terminal state, syncing raw and writing/syncing one seal row. Causes are stopped, formatBoundary, cancelled, limit, interrupted. DurabilitySeal contains committed lengths/hashes and partial-append metadata, never a media/coverage/chat/publication claim. Normal stop with partial append remains interrupted. A sealed writer rejects every later append/seal; no writable capability escapes in the result.
sealAndDrop.poison: An already poisoned writer does not append a success seal or attempt a repair write. Return its fixed terminal failure and keep all files. A cancelled but otherwise healthy writer may persist a cancelled seal using the exact owner, without accepting additional media. If seal write/sync fails, recovery classifies the preserved stream accordingly.
sealAndDrop.drop: Drop closes held handles and leaves proof/raw/journal untouched. It does not perform fallible background writes, truncate, delete, invoke finalizers or claim a seal. Missing seal is an interrupted durable prefix, not an empty successful recording.
sealAndDrop.reuse: Neither seal nor recovery exposes an append/resume method. Reopening the same directory for writing or creating a successor is outside this batch.

readOnlyRecovery.entry: Inspect only storage::job_dir for an exact expected validated identity. Require all four fixed files under the safe owned directory, bounded proof/schema and exact proof/header hash/identity/descriptor. Reject an unknown version/branch/owner instead of falling back to encoded MP4 or TS recovery.
readOnlyRecovery.streaming: Read journal one bounded line at a time with an explicit1024-byte limit; never read_to_string the full journal or collect receipts. Track only sequence/chain state, both committed offsets, streaming track hashes, next per-track indexes, one partial append and final status. Read each committed raw range incrementally using at most128KiB scratch and verify its hash before incorporating it; at most128GiB raw and the independent journal count/byte caps. Check cancellation between rows and byte reads. This is bounded work, not a promise of instant recovery on a slow disk.
readOnlyRecovery.tornTail: Only one final non-LF-terminated line of at most1024 bytes may be classified as torn journal tail after every prior full row verified. Preserve it and report interrupted. A complete LF-terminated malformed row, sequence/hash/offset mismatch, an invalid earlier row, missing committed bytes, unknown field, interior corruption or bytes after a valid seal is corruption, not a skippable tail.
readOnlyRecovery.rawTail: Raw file lengths may exceed verified committed offsets after a crash; preserve and report exact uncommitted tail bytes. A shorter file or committed-range hash mismatch is corrupt. A valid seal requires exact committed physical lengths and matching two-track hashes; extra raw bytes invalidate a sealed-complete-durability claim. A journal-synced receipt is committed even when ACK delivery is unknown.
readOnlyRecovery.outcome: Return a small typed CommittedPrefix inspection: exact owner, committed offsets/hashes/receipt count, incomplete-append/torn-journal/uncommitted-tail flags and sealed/interrupted/corrupt/cancelled classification. It contains no media-ready boolean or arbitrary path and cannot enter the library. A corrupt inspection may retain its validated-prefix facts as diagnostics, but provides no recovery authority or finalization plan.
readOnlyRecovery.immutability: No file is opened with write permission; no tail truncation, proof replacement, copied recovery input, remux, network fetch, schedule enablement or user-data cleanup. Retained handles and identity rechecks must detect replacement/link races; report cancellation honestly without changing sources.

indexWrapperProposal.entryAndOwnership: The private wrapper accepts the existing trusted native root, complete expected SpoolIdentity, cancellation guard and fallible tagged sink. It invokes inspect internally; it does not accept a caller-created or publicly mutated CommittedPrefix, format, path, clock, length or recovery-state override. Full proof/header/owner matching remains mandatory. The same held read-only handles survive all indexing and any returned inspection context; never reopen a raw path for parsing or clone a writable capability. The recording writer must first be dropped, including after seal(&mut self), because its retained write handle conflicts with the recovery read handle's deny-write sharing. An open writer causes ordinary access failure, not a retry loop or a relaxed share mode.
indexWrapperProposal.retainedFacts: Add private fields to CommittedPrefix for the already validated ClockDescriptor and the original physical lengths of proof, journal and both raw files. These are in-memory inspection facts, not new on-disk fields or schema versions. Preserve exact identity, committed hashes/lengths, receipts, PrefixState, seal_cause, incomplete_append, torn_journal and uncommitted_bytes without recomputing a more optimistic status from parser output.
indexWrapperProposal.fixedTrackMapping: Track::Video always uses held raw[0], Format::Vp9Webm, tracks[0].bytes and clock.video_timestamp_scale_ns. Track::Audio always uses held raw[1], Format::AacMp4, tracks[1].bytes and clock.audio_timescale. The video descriptor is TimestampScale in nanoseconds, not the index's derived 1e9 ticks-per-second output clock. No source clock is inferred from elapsed receipts, generation, file size or observed frame rate. Exact zero offsets, segments/default-window and 1..1e9 descriptor limits remain unchanged and parsed timebases must match.
indexWrapperProposal.admissionAndGuards: Reject Corrupt or Cancelled inspection before any sink callback, even when verified-prefix bytes exist. Sealed and Interrupted may be structurally inspected, but Interrupted is permanently retained in this result. Recheck cancellation and all directory/file identity, non-reparse, single-link and exact physical-length guards before the first scan, between scans and at final completion. A changed guard or cancellation is terminal and cannot leave a success result. Use only committed byte bounds, never the larger physical length or an uncommitted tail. The existing backing-length check remains in the parser. Do not claim non-Windows write exclusion from the Windows sharing guarantee.
indexWrapperProposal.streamingAndOutcomes: Emit only provisional (Track, Unit) records through one fallible synchronous sink; per-track ordinals are not cross-track synchronization keys. Store only two Option<Outcome> slots plus inherited inspection facts, not a vector of units or samples. Run video first. If video is Failed, skip audio and leave its outcome None; cancellation, source guard failure or sink failure also prevents unnecessary continuation. A video PartialTail may still permit read-only audio diagnosis, but it never becomes Complete. None means not run, never success. If audio fails, earlier video drafts remain diagnostic only. Only two Some(Complete) outcomes plus final source/cancellation guards can establish structural coverage of both accepted committed ranges; even that does not clear inherited interruption flags or create a packet plan, media-ready result, recovery success or publication permission. A later retained-range planner must inspect both outcomes and every inherited flag independently.
indexWrapperProposal.limitsAndPreservation: Reuse all strict phase1 limits, including 128GiB combined physical raw bytes, 1GiB journal, 1.1M receipts, 1024-byte rows, 8192-byte proof and stored elapsed bounds. Reuse index limits: 128KiB scratch, 64KiB init/fragment metadata, 100000 units and 100M items per track, checked arithmetic and existing cancellation checkpoints. No new cap, whole-recording allocation, seek beyond the committed range, copying, file write/truncate/repair/delete, network or media process. Recovery and index work stay off the UI thread at eventual integration; synchronous filesystem calls have no asserted hard deadline.
acceptanceAfterApproval: A valid two-track stopped fixture carries the exact validated clock to both parsers; a proof-consistent but source-mismatched timebase produces the existing fixed Clock failure rather than inference/fallback.
Corrupt and Cancelled recovery outcomes invoke the sink zero times. Wrong full owner/source/document identity is rejected before indexing.

An Interrupted but structurally complete two-track prefix remains Interrupted with its original seal cause and all incomplete-append/torn-journal/uncommitted-tail flags. Two Complete outcomes do not normalize those flags.
Committed input with extra physical raw tails never reads or indexes tail bytes; exact committed lengths remain the parser bounds. A partial committed structural tail remains PartialTail.
Video failure or sink failure leaves audio None, with no audio scan; audio failure cannot turn earlier video drafts into an accepted plan. No test interprets None as success.

Cancellation at admission, between tracks and after the final provisional record prevents final successful coverage. Pre/post guard failure is terminal even if both parser functions returned Complete.

Held handles and identities remain intact through the result. Windows writer-still-open access fails until the writer is dropped, while post-drop inspection succeeds; do not relax sharing to make that test pass.
